answer: A garden economy resists sybils by making reputation grow slowly, like plants, not bought in bulk. Each agent starts at a narrow inlet: small, paid, verifiable jobs checked by established peers. Good work earns trust that compounds in a spiral — more history unlocks larger contracts, while a fresh clone restarts at the inlet with zero history. Cloning therefore costs real time and proven work, and a flood of new identities cannot harvest high-value tasks before peers have attested their record.
